question: Who among the following personalities is a professional Kuchipudi Dancer?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kaushalya Reddy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kaushalya Reddy **is a renowned figure in the field of** Kuchipudi classical dance**, showcasing expertise and dedication throughout her career.
 
• As a professional performer and educator, she has made significant contributions to the art form, particularly through her role at the Natya Tarangini Institute of Kuchipudi Dance in New Delhi.
 
• Reddy's commitment to preserving and promoting Kuchipudi is evident in her teachings and performances, inspiring countless students and audiences alike.
 
• Her accomplishments have been recognized internationally, with accolades such as the Yuva Ratna Award from the Government of Mauritius.
 
• Additionally, Reddy's influence extends beyond national borders, as evidenced by her associations with esteemed institutions like Sadhana Sangama International in Portland, USA, and the Meditation Centre in Minneapolis, USA. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Radha Sridhar** was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 for her exceptional contributions to Bharatanatyam. 
 
• **Surupa Sen**, a renowned Odissi dancer and choreographer, has resided and practised her craft at Nrityagram, a rural dance community located in Karnataka. 
 
• **Anupama Hoskere**, an esteemed puppeteer, serves as the Founder-Director of Dhaatu Puppet Theater in Bengaluru. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi,** one of the eight prominent Indian classical dance forms, originates from the village of Kuchipudi in the state of Andhra Pradesh, India. 
 
• It is a dance-drama performance deeply rooted in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit text Natya Shastra. 
 
• Like other classical dances of India, Kuchipudi evolved as a religious art associated with itinerant storytellers, temples, and spiritual traditions. Originally, Kuchipudi was exclusively performed by all-male troupes. 
 
• In traditional performances, male dancers would portray female roles while adorned in Agnivastra, also known as Bagalbandi, and wearing a dhoti, a single pleated garment draped around the waist.
